original_claim: TEDS-A (through 2023): heroin's share of primary-opioid admissions fell and 'other opiates & synthetics' rose, mainly from 2021.
supported_claim: From 2019 to 2024, heroin's share of primary-opioid admissions changed by -33.3 percentage points and the 'other opiates & synthetics' share by +33.4 points in the 35-state panel.
main_caveat: Code 7 combines fentanyl, prescription opioids and buprenorphine (no fentanyl-specific code); admissions are treatment episodes at publicly funded facilities, not people or prevalence.

original_claim: TEDS-A (through 2023): first-time primary-opioid admissions per 100k fell at ages 18-24.
supported_claim: First-time primary-opioid admissions per 100k people aged 18-24 changed by -53% from 2019 to 2024 (lower bound; -54% upper bound) in the 35-state panel, and by -43% without states flagged for prior-treatment coding shifts.
main_caveat: First-time admissions are not new cases of addiction (they also reflect access, capacity and time from onset to treatment). 2019 lies inside a 2018-2020 prior-treatment coding artifact driven by California; the coding-shift-excluded sensitivity addresses this.

original_claim: TEDS-A (through 2023): from 2019, opioid deaths rose relative to primary-opioid admissions.
supported_claim: From 2019 to 2024, opioid deaths changed by +12% and primary-opioid admissions by -39% in the 28-state deaths panel.
main_caveat: Admissions track treatment entry at publicly funded facilities (funding, capacity, 2020 disruption, office-based buprenorphine not captured); deaths are mostly illicitly made fentanyl.

original_claim: (new) 2023 -> 2024, the first TEDS-A year overlapping the decline in overdose deaths.
supported_claim: From 2023 to 2024, opioid deaths changed by -32% and primary-opioid admissions by -7%; the opioid death rate fell relative to the admission rate.
main_caveat: A single year; the 2024 TEDS-A file excludes South Carolina and Washington (neither is in the panel).
